title: observability: attach stream-fragment anchors and function-event-jsonl with endpoint-fingerprint
author: Maya Chen
commits: introduce stream fragment anchor id & endpoint fingerprint (Maya)
emit function-call events as compact jsonl envelope (Maya)
openai-compat: include x-rwi-fingerprint header when present (Lena)
tests: add fragment-reassembly and sampling tests (Arjun)
description:
Motivation: Streaming clients and backend tooling have become fragile for traces that cross the API surface, tool executors, and the streaming reassembly layer. Existing request IDs are useful but not sufficient for sampling-friendly correlation of partial stream fragments, in-flight function/tool call events, and per-endpoint cost/latency breakdowns. This PR adds a lightweight per-fragment 'anchor' and an endpoint fingerprint header to make logs and metrics easier to join without changing the external OpenAI-compatible payloads for clients that don't opt in.

What this change does: 1) Stream fragment anchors: the fragmenter emits a short stable anchor token (8 hex chars) for each stream fragment series; anchors are included in JSONL access logs and in the streaming wire envelope as "rwi_anchor" metadata when clients negotiate observability. 2) Endpoint fingerprint: a compact, non-sensitive hash of (route, method, model-variant) is computed and added as the X-RWI-Fingerprint header internally and surfaced in logs/metrics as endpoint_fingerprint. This lets per-endpoint metrics group without exposing full route names in lower-trust sinks. 3) Function-call event JSONL: when a function/tool call is started/completed within a streamed response, we emit a single-line JSONL envelope that contains the anchor, trace id, func name, duration_ms, status, and a small size token. This is intended for high-cardinality, low-latency ingestion into observability pipelines. 4) OpenAI-compat shim: behavior is backward compatible by default; legacy clients see no schema change. The OpenAI-compat middleware will inject anchor metadata only if either the client supplies X-RWI-Enable or if the server-side config allows sampling.

Implementation notes: - fragmenter.go: new fragment anchor generator (crypto/rand truncated, with deterministic testing stubbed) and wire-level envelope annotation. - jsonl_writer.go: compact writer that uses buffered writes and optional truncation of very large payload fields (max_field_bytes configurable). - compat_shim.go: detects client opt-in and maps rwi fields to the openai-shim metadata header. - configs/obs/defaults.yaml: default sampling rate 0.01 and allowlist of internal sinks. - tests: added deterministic fragment reassembly test and an integration test that asserts anchor presence through the OpenAI-compat path.

Backward compatibility & rollout: Default behavior is off for customers who haven't enabled observability sampling. We will release this behind a runtime flag 'obs.enable_stream_anchors' and incrementally enable for internal customers and a small canary cohort. If issues arise, we can toggle the flag and revert the shim mapping without rolling back the runtime binary.

Telemetry schema (summary): - anchor: string (8 hex) - trace_id: existing request span id - endpoint_fingerprint: string (6-8 chars) - func_event: {name, phase: start|end, duration_ms, status} emitted as JSONL envelope

Notes for reviewers: I focused on minimizing per-token overhead in the hot path; the fragment anchor is generated once per logical stream (not per token). The JSONL writer is designed to be append-only to avoid locking hot-path token rendering. See docs/observability/streaming-anchors.md for usage and example parsers.
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we stable-hash the endpoint fingerprint so it survives minor route refactors? If we change the route name the fingerprint should be intentionally different — for now we hash (service, route_id, model_variant) as discussed.
Maya Chen (author): We'll keep the hash inputs explicit, added a comment and a unit test to ensure stability across unrelated code moves.
Lena Rodrigues: Danger: large function payloads might bloat JSONL. Are we truncating user-supplied arguments?
Maya Chen (author): Yes, jsonl_writer.go truncates large fields to configs.obs.max_field_bytes (default 1024). Added a test and telemetry counter for truncated fields.
Diego Marquez: CI flaky on the streaming integration, re-run?
Arjun Patel: re-ran integration pipeline, flakes fixed by increasing test buffer timeout from 200ms to 500ms.
release_notes:
- Added optional stream fragment anchors for better cross-service tracing and sampling.
- Endpoint fingerprints for compact per-route metrics grouping.
- Function-call / tool-call events emitted as single-line JSONL envelopes for low-latency observability ingestion.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover anchor generation and fingerprint stability. Integration tests validate anchor propagation through OpenAI-compat shim and fragment reassembly. Load test showed <0.5% CPU overhead at 5k rps with anchors enabled at 1% sampling. Manual validation performed with internal canary (team: infra-platform).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag 'obs.enable_stream_anchors' (default false). 2) Enable for internal infra-platform + 3 pilot customers at 1% sampling. 3) Monitor error rates and ingest QPS for JSONL sink. 4) Gradually increase sampling to 5% and optionally enable for broader cohort. 5) If issues, flip flag off and investigate.
notes_for_ops: Observe JSONL sink QPS and per-ingest cost after enabling. There is a config knob configs/obs/max_field_bytes to control ingest size. If the JSONL sink lags, reduce sampling or toggle allowlist to internal-only.
